images.caption: Gavin Maxwell's grave at Sandaig Gavin Maxwell,(1914-1969), was many things; an army officer during WWII, shark fisherman, explorer, naturalist and author. He came to live here studying the otters which he kept and writing about them - Edal and Teko amongst them. His best known book is undoubtedly 'Ring of Bright Water', which was made into an award winning film and set here. In the book and film he changed the name of Sandaig to Camusfeàrna. When he died his ashes were buried here and a plaque erected on this boulder.

images.caption: Above Kirkmaiden Church and overlooking Front Bay near the village of Monreith is the bronze otter, sculpted by Penny Wheatley, standing as a memorial to Gavin Maxwell, the author of the famous book "Ring of Bright Water", which was also made into a successful film. Gavin Maxwell was often seen exercising his tame otter, about which he wrote his book, on the beach below Kirkmaiden church, when he returned to the area.

images.caption:
This is located at Sandaig (Camusfearna) on Scotland's West Coast close to where naturalist writer Gavin Maxwell wrote the book "Ring of Bright Water" - and others - about his life here with otters.

In 1968 Maxwell's house was completely burned down in a devastating fire. That Night it was necessary for Maxwell, his companions and surviving otter to take refuge in this cottage as this is a remote spot and there was nowhere also to go.

images.caption:
This is the location of the writer Gavin Maxwell's home on the West Coast of Scotland where he wrote such books as "Ring of bright Water", "Raven Seek thy Brother" and "The Rocks Remain".

He called this place Camusfearna - it's real name is Sandaig, near Glenelg. The mountains on the Isle of Skye are in the background.

images.caption:
On the exact spot where the writer Gavin Maxwell's desk stood is this memorial stone (under which his ashes were scattered)
The house was destroyed by fire a year or so before he died.
The plaque reads:
"Beneath this stone
the site of Camusfearna
are buried the ashes of 
Gavin Maxwell
b. 15th July 1914

d 7th September 1969"

images.caption:
When the house of writer Gavin Maxwell which was called Camusfearna, on the West coast of Scotland, burned down the Otter Edal was killed. 
Nearby she was buried and this memorial erected. It reads:
"EDAL THE OTTER OF RING OF BRIGHT WATER
1958-1968. Whatever joy she gave to you, give back to nature. GAVIN MAXWELL."

He also died, a year later, and his ashes are buried close by.

images.caption:
The house known as Camusfearna stood to the right of this picture (behind the trees). The only thing there now is the memorial stone to Gavin Maxwell.

This photo (and others i'm uploading) may be of particular interest to a specific group of people: Fans of the Books by Gavin Maxwell, and specifically those relating to his pet otters - the trilogy of "Ring of Bright Water"; "Raven seek thy Brother" and "The Rocks remain".  

The books were hugely popular and sold millions. The location of his "Camusfearna" remained mostly unknown until the house burned down in 1968. For the vast majority of people the site is too remote to visit (even if they wanted to).

Living in Scotland, I was able to visit Sandaig (its' real name) in 1977 and again in 2011.   Now, 50 years after the fire I've decided to post a selection of my pictures of Sandaig and nearby on Flickr. For anyone interested the pictures will be in my "RoBW"  folder.
